note: Single source for the coverage matrix (docs/coverage-matrix.md) and the panel's rules page. CoverageCatalogTest fails if a registered collector is missing here. Detection windows are typical defaults, not guarantees.

modules.name: Files on disk
modules.privileges: Administrator for raw NTFS/MFT reads; without it a slower filesystem walk sees only what the user can list.
sources: NTFS master file table of every fixed drive (names)
Content of binaries in user-writable locations: SHA-256, embedded CS2 offset strings, PE imports, alternate data streams, entropy
kinds: DETECTION: SHA-256 equals a classified sample
INDICATOR: name, strings (a single game field name alone is LOW and does not ask for review), imports, disguised PE, entropy
modules.window: Files present at the moment of the scan.
modules.lookalikes: Game-modding tools, overlays, trainers for single-player games, and packers used by legitimate software share names, imports and high entropy. Legitimate Source-engine tools (demo and movie tools, server plugins, SDK code) contain the game's own field names, so one field name alone is only shown as LOW; offset-dump names or several names together ask for review.
modules.blindSpots: Anything not on a fixed NTFS drive at scan time (removable media, network shares, memory-only payloads, renamed and re-hashed builds of a known cheat).

modules.name: Deleted and renamed files
modules.privileges: Administrator (USN journal is read through the volume handle).
sources: NTFS USN change journal delete/rename records
kinds: INDICATOR: a deleted/renamed file whose name matches a signature
modules.window: USN journal: size-bound, typically days to a few weeks on a system drive. Recycle Bin: until emptied.
modules.lookalikes: Legitimate uninstallers and updaters delete files with similar names.
modules.blindSpots: Journal already wrapped or deleted (the concealment collector reports a reset), files deleted on other volumes, content of deleted files (names only).

modules.name: Execution history
modules.privileges: Administrator for other users' hives and the Prefetch folder.
kinds: INDICATOR: a program that matches a signature was executed
modules.window: Prefetch: last ~1024 programs, 8 run times each (disabled by default on Windows Server). BAM: about one week. The others: until cleared.
modules.lookalikes: A program with a matching name is not necessarily the cheat; name-only evidence.
modules.blindSpots: Execution from memory without an image on disk, Prefetch disabled, artefacts wiped (reported by the concealment collector when detectable).

modules.name: AmCache
modules.privileges: Administrator (Amcache.hve is locked; mounted from a copy).
sources: Amcache.hve file and driver inventory (path, SHA-1 of the first 30 MB)
kinds: INDICATOR: path/name match of a program or driver seen by Windows
modules.window: Months; survives deletion of the file itself.
modules.lookalikes: Name matches only; the stored SHA-1 is not compared against the SHA-256 sample set.
modules.blindSpots: Hive reset or deleted, programs never inventoried by Windows.

modules.name: Startup and scheduled tasks
modules.privileges: Administrator for all users' Run keys, services and tasks.
kinds: INDICATOR: autostart entry launching a signature match or running from Temp/Public/Recycle Bin/drive root
modules.lookalikes: Game launchers, RGB and peripheral software autostart from unusual folders.
modules.blindSpots: One-shot loaders that never register autostart, WMI subscriptions and other rarer persistence points.

modules.name: Kernel state
modules.privileges: Administrator/root. With the Moon kernel component loaded it also reads the kernel's own module/task lists.
sources: Windows: loaded kernel services, boot options (SystemStartOptions), platform security settings (Secure Boot, memory integrity, VBS, vulnerable-driver blocklist, TPM); optional MoonMon.sys report
Linux: /proc/modules, kernel taint, /etc/ld.so.preload, Secure Boot, lockdown, module signing, ptrace scope; optional moonmon.ko task list
kinds: INDICATOR: vulnerable/mapper driver in a user-writable or unusual folder, cheat driver name, ld.so.preload injection
CONCEALMENT: object hidden from one view
CONFIGURATION: test signing, weakened boot integrity, vulnerable-driver blocklist turned off
CONTEXT: vulnerable driver installed by software in a Windows or program folder, platform security settings, tainted kernel
modules.lookalikes: MSI Afterburner, RGB/fan-control utilities, motherboard suites and other games' anti-cheats install drivers that are on vulnerable-driver lists; installed in Windows or program folders they are context only. NVIDIA's proprietary driver taints most Linux gaming kernels.
modules.blindSpots: Manually mapped drivers are absent from every module list, including the kernel component's; firmware, hypervisor and DMA-based cheats are outside what a guest OS can observe.

modules.name: Processes, drivers and hardware
modules.privileges: Administrator to read other processes' image paths.
sources: PC summary (CPU, GPU, RAM, board, monitors, uptime)
kinds: INDICATOR: process/window/PCI device matches
CONFIGURATION: virtual machine
CONTEXT: vulnerable driver installed by software
modules.window: Processes and devices present during the scan.
modules.lookalikes: Window titles and process names are trivially renamed and can collide with legitimate tools; FPGA/PCIe development boards match DMA patterns.
modules.blindSpots: Cheats not running during the scan; DMA hardware that impersonates an ordinary device ID.

modules.name: Signs of cleaning
modules.privileges: Administrator for the Security event log and system settings.
sources: Recent OS reinstall (told apart from a feature update)
Cleaner tools: installed, ran, ran in the last 24 hours, running
kinds: CONCEALMENT: evidence was removed or collection was disabled; a cleaner run in the last day or running now
CONTEXT: recent Windows feature update
modules.window: Varies per source; event logs are size-bound.
modules.lookalikes: Privacy-minded users run cleaners and many PCs ship with one installed (installed or run long ago is LOW context); a Windows feature update rewrites the install date like a reinstall would, and is told apart by the Setup\Source OS keys.
modules.blindSpots: Careful cleaning that leaves no meta-trace.

modules.name: CS2 installation integrity
modules.privileges: Read access to the Steam library.
sources: Foreign or unsigned binaries in CS2 bin directories
kinds: INDICATOR: tampering with the game's load paths, foreign binaries, VAC-disabling launch options
modules.lookalikes: Workshop map makers and community-server developers modify the install; some overlays drop DLLs next to games.
modules.blindSpots: Cheats that never touch the install (external or kernel readers); per-file verification against Steam's depot manifest is not implemented yet.

modules.name: Running game
modules.privileges: Administrator, to read the module list of cs2.exe. Needs CS2 running.
sources: Visible top-level windows: style, position, owning process
kinds: INDICATOR: DLL from a user or unusual folder loaded into CS2, cheat-named module, transparent always-on-top window over the game owned by an unknown program
CONTEXT: overlays and program modules in the game, CS2 not running
modules.window: While the check runs; only if CS2 is running.
modules.lookalikes: Steam, Discord, NVIDIA, AMD, RivaTuner (MSI Afterburner), OBS, Overwolf and Medal inject overlays and draw over the game; they are listed as context. A portable tool run from Downloads can load a DLL too.
modules.blindSpots: Manually mapped DLLs are absent from the module list; an ESP drawn through a DirectX hook has no window; nothing when CS2 is closed.

modules.name: Browser history matches
modules.privileges: User; administrator to read other profiles.
sources: Chromium-family and Firefox history databases — only URLs matching the signature domain list leave the PC
kinds: INDICATOR: visits to listed domains (count, most recent)
modules.lookalikes: Visiting a site is not using a product; reviews, news and anti-cheat research land on the same domains.
modules.blindSpots: Private windows, other browsers, cleared history.

modules.name: Steam accounts
sources: Public VAC status from the Steam Community profile XML (network request per account)
kinds: CONTEXT: accounts on this PC, VAC history
modules.window: Accounts ever remembered by this Steam client.
modules.lookalikes: Shared family PCs have several accounts.
modules.blindSpots: Accounts used on other PCs; VAC status is history, not evidence of current cheating.

modules.name: Macro software and USB history
sources: Installed programs, processes and scripts of macro tools
kinds: INDICATOR/CONTEXT: macro software present, removable storage used
modules.window: Installed state; USB history persists in the registry.
modules.lookalikes: Gaming-mouse vendor software ships macro engines by default.
modules.blindSpots: Hardware macros stored on the device itself.

modules.name: Windows Defender history
kinds: INDICATOR: past game-hack, cheat-engine, trainer or HackTool DLL-injector detections
CONFIGURATION: real-time protection turned off by a setting
CONTEXT: other HackTool detections (activators, keygens, cracks)
CONCEALMENT: exclusions of user-writable folders, whole drives or all programs
CONTEXT: exclusions of program, game or tools folders
modules.lookalikes: Defender files Windows/Office activators, keygens and cracks under HackTool; they are software piracy, not game hacking, and are only context. Many gamers turn real-time protection off for performance.
modules.blindSpots: PCs using another antivirus; history purged.

modules.name: DNS cache
kinds: INDICATOR: a cheat site the PC looked up recently
CONTEXT: how many names were checked
modules.window: Minutes to about a day (each record's lifetime); emptied by a restart or ipconfig /flushdns.
modules.lookalikes: Opening a cheat site out of curiosity, a link in a chat; a match says the PC contacted the site, not why.
modules.blindSpots: Flushed or restarted caches; DNS-over-HTTPS in browsers bypasses the Windows cache.

modules.name: Linux processes
modules.privileges: Root to read other users' /proc entries and the CS2 process's maps.
sources: CS2 process: memory maps, environment (LD_PRELOAD, deleted or temp-path libraries)
kinds: INDICATOR: signature matches, injected or deleted libraries in CS2
modules.window: During the scan; CS2 must be running for the in-game checks.
modules.lookalikes: Overlays (MangoHud, OBS vkcapture) inject via LD_PRELOAD legitimately.
modules.blindSpots: External readers that use ptrace/process_vm_readv only while the game runs and exit before the scan — only continuous monitoring could see them.

modules.name: Linux files
modules.privileges: Root to read every home directory.
sources: Home folders, .local/share, .steam, /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm — content inspection shared with the Windows collector
kinds: DETECTION: SHA-256 equals a classified sample
INDICATOR: strings, ELF/PE content, entropy
modules.lookalikes: As for the Windows file collector.
modules.blindSpots: Locations outside the listed roots; memfd-only payloads.

modules.name: Linux browser and shell history
kinds: INDICATOR: listed domains, download or execution of a signature match
modules.lookalikes: Research and news visits; history lines are unauthenticated text.

modules.name: Linux autostart
kinds: INDICATOR: autostart of a signature match, LD_PRELOAD or curl|bash lines
modules.lookalikes: Developers keep LD_PRELOAD and curl|bash in shell configs.
modules.blindSpots: System-wide units, udev rules, other persistence points.

rules.meaning: The file's SHA-256 equals a sample a maintainer classified as a cheat.
rules.lookalikes: None for the exact file; a hash identifies content, not who put it there.
rules.limits: Possession, not proof of use. Any rebuild of the cheat has a new hash.

rules.meaning: The checker ran inside a virtual machine.
rules.lookalikes: Players testing the checker; the gaming PC may be a different machine.
rules.limits: Lowers assurance: the inspected system may not be the one used to play.

rules.meaning: Boot options weaken kernel integrity (e.g. integrity checks disabled).
rules.lookalikes: Debugging setups, old tweak guides.
rules.limits: Lowers assurance; never a verdict.

rules.meaning: Driver signature enforcement is off.
rules.lookalikes: Driver development.
rules.limits: Lowers assurance; never a verdict.

rules.meaning: The Linux kernel reports taint flags.
rules.lookalikes: NVIDIA's proprietary driver on almost every gaming PC.
rules.limits: Context only.

rules.meaning: A process the Linux kernel component lists is absent from /proc, re-checked after the diff.
rules.lookalikes: PID namespaces (the checker running inside a container) and races the re-check did not catch.
rules.limits: Reported only for a PID that answers at /proc/<pid> with the same name while two listings of /proc leave it out (exited, newly started and reused PIDs are races, not hiding). Kernel-mode rootkits hide from both views.

rules.meaning: A Windows kernel module was loaded from outside the Windows folder (from the kernel component's module list).
rules.lookalikes: Anti-cheats of other games, VPN, virtualisation and peripheral drivers under Program Files.
rules.limits: LOW severity: listed for the reviewer, never a reason to review on its own.

rules.meaning: A kernel module appears in one view and not another.
rules.lookalikes: Modules loading or unloading during the scan.
rules.limits: Review required.

rules.meaning: An account that logged in on this PC has a VAC ban on record.
rules.lookalikes: Shared PCs, bought second-hand accounts.
rules.limits: History, not evidence of current cheating.

rules.meaning: Several Steam accounts have logged in on this PC.
rules.lookalikes: Family PCs, internet cafés.
rules.limits: Context only.

rules.meaning: A driver on the vulnerable/mapper list sits in a user-writable folder (Temp, AppData, Downloads, Desktop) or an unusual one — where a cheat loader drops a driver it abuses (BYOVD).
rules.lookalikes: A portable hardware tool run from Downloads can load its driver from there.
rules.limits: User-writable location: the rule's severity. Unusual location: MEDIUM. A manual-mapper name is never legitimate.

rules.meaning: A driver on the vulnerable list is installed in a Windows or program folder by the software it belongs to (MSI Afterburner, RGB and fan-control tools, motherboard suites, another game's anti-cheat).
rules.lookalikes: This is the lookalike: everyday gaming software.
rules.limits: Context only; the same driver in a user folder is kernel:vulnerable-driver.

rules.meaning: Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist was switched off (VulnerableDriverBlocklistEnable=0).
rules.lookalikes: Some old hardware tools ask users to turn it off.
rules.limits: Lowers the assurance of the scan; never a verdict.

rules.meaning: The PC's security settings in one line: Secure Boot, memory integrity, VBS, vulnerable-driver blocklist and TPM on Windows; Secure Boot, lockdown, module signing and ptrace scope on Linux.
rules.lookalikes: Most gaming PCs run with some of these off.
rules.limits: Context for the reviewer; says how much a kernel-level cheat would have to defeat.

rules.meaning: A file carries a hidden NTFS stream: named like a cheat (CRITICAL), large enough to hold a program (≥32 KiB, HIGH), otherwise small (LOW).
rules.lookalikes: Windows, browsers, antivirus and sync tools write small streams (Zone.Identifier, SmartScreen, KAVICHS, Dropbox, Mac metadata) — these are skipped while small.
rules.limits: Unknown streams are reported wherever the file lives; in a system or program folder with an unverified publisher they are low-weight context. A verified publisher or approved hash silences the heuristic part; cheat-named streams are always CRITICAL.

rules.meaning: Windows Defender's history holds a detection of a game hack, cheat engine, trainer or HackTool DLL injector, or a file whose path matches a cheat rule.
rules.lookalikes: Single-player trainers are MEDIUM.
rules.limits: Only what Defender saw and recorded; a history cleared by the user is empty.

rules.meaning: Defender recorded a HackTool that is not about games: Windows/Office activators, keygens, cracks.
rules.lookalikes: Software piracy is common and unrelated to cheating in CS2.
rules.limits: Context only.

rules.meaning: Defender real-time protection is turned off by a setting.
rules.lookalikes: Many gamers turn it off for performance; a third-party antivirus does not change this setting.
rules.limits: Lowers the assurance of the scan; never a verdict.

rules.meaning: Windows was installed in the last 7 days and there is no sign of an in-place upgrade.
rules.lookalikes: A new PC or a reinstall after a hardware change.
rules.limits: MEDIUM: asks for a look.

rules.meaning: Windows was upgraded in place in the last 7 days (feature update), which rewrites the install date.
rules.lookalikes: This is the lookalike of a reinstall.
rules.limits: Context only: history from before the update may be shorter.

rules.meaning: CS2 is set to start with an option that lowers protection: -insecure (VAC off), -allow_third_party_software, -tools, -nosteam.
rules.lookalikes: Map makers use -tools; offline practice and demo tools use -insecure or allow third-party software.
rules.limits: Lowers the assurance of the scan; never a verdict.

rules.meaning: A program library in CS2's bin folders carries no code signature.
rules.lookalikes: CS2 ships some third-party libraries; compare the name with a clean install.
rules.limits: LOW until measured on real installs; the check sees whether a certificate is present, not whose it is.

rules.meaning: A CS2 config contains a movement or fire script pattern (bunny-hop, jumpthrow, auto-fire alias).
rules.lookalikes: Practice configs and scroll-jump binds are common and allowed on many servers.
rules.limits: LOW: shown to the reviewer; the server's own rules decide.

rules.meaning: A module loaded into cs2.exe is named like a cheat.
rules.lookalikes: None expected.
rules.limits: CRITICAL; a renamed cheat is caught by the folder rules instead.

rules.meaning: A DLL loaded into cs2.exe comes from Temp, Downloads, the Desktop, AppData or another user folder — how most internal cheats get in.
rules.lookalikes: Overlays that live in AppData (Discord, Overwolf, Medal) pass only when their publisher is verified (valid signature, pinned root, exact vendor name); a familiar DLL name alone does not.
rules.limits: HIGH; manually mapped cheats do not appear in the module list.

rules.meaning: A DLL loaded into cs2.exe comes from a folder that is not the game's, Windows' or a program folder.
rules.lookalikes: A tool installed to its own folder on another drive.
rules.limits: MEDIUM: asks for a look.

rules.meaning: Overlays and program libraries loaded into the game, listed for the reviewer.
rules.lookalikes: This is the lookalike list.
rules.limits: Context only.

rules.meaning: A transparent, always-on-top window covers the game and belongs to a program that is not a known overlay — the shape of an external ESP.
rules.lookalikes: Steam, Discord, NVIDIA, AMD, RivaTuner, OBS and Windows shell overlays pass only with a known program name AND a verified publisher; an unverified one is reported with a note.
rules.limits: MEDIUM (HIGH from a user folder); ESPs drawn through a DirectX hook have no window.

rules.meaning: CS2 was not running, so the live checks did not run.
rules.limits: Ask the player to start CS2 and run the check again to see what is loaded into the game.

rules.meaning: A Windows library name (version.dll, dxgi.dll, winmm.dll…) is loaded into cs2.exe from the game folder instead of System32 — DLL proxying, a way into the game without an injector.
rules.lookalikes: Some games ship their own copies of such libraries; CS2 does not. A verified publisher clears it.
rules.limits: MEDIUM; only libraries loaded at the moment of the check; a proxy that unloads itself is not seen.

rules.meaning: What the Windows file scan covered: drives indexed by name, files in user folders, outcomes (inspected, not an executable, too large, unreadable, cloud-only), the whole-drive content pass and what it skipped.
rules.limits: Never changes the outcome; required parts that could not be covered make the collector PARTIAL instead.

rules.meaning: What the Linux file scan covered: files in the required folders, outcomes, the excluded Steam-library and Flatpak folders and how much of them was walked afterwards.
rules.limits: Never changes the outcome; a required folder that could not be read completely makes the collector PARTIAL.

rules.meaning: An ELF program in a scanned folder refers to process_vm_readv / process_vm_writev — reading or writing another process's memory, what external Linux cheats do.
rules.lookalikes: Debuggers, profilers and game-modding tools use the same calls.
rules.limits: LOW alone; MEDIUM together with CS2 offset strings. Static reference only: a program can resolve the call at run time.

rules.meaning: The optional Moon kernel component's view was compared with the user-mode view (records compared, discrepancies left after re-checking races).
rules.limits: An empty discrepancy list is not proof of a clean kernel: kernel-mode rootkits, manually mapped drivers, hypervisors and DMA devices are invisible to both views.

rules.meaning: The Moon kernel component is installed but this run could not open it (not elevated).
rules.limits: Nothing was compared; the user-mode checks ran.

rules.meaning: An antivirus exclusion of a program, game or tools folder, a file type or a process.
rules.lookalikes: Games, IDEs and build tools are often excluded for speed.
rules.limits: Never changes the outcome.

rules.meaning: Windows Defender is told not to scan a folder an ordinary user can write to (Downloads, AppData, Temp, Desktop…).
rules.lookalikes: Some players exclude a downloads or mods folder; ask why.
rules.limits: MEDIUM; the exclusion list itself, not what is in the folder.

rules.meaning: A whole drive is excluded from antivirus scanning.
rules.lookalikes: Rare; some users do it for speed on a games drive.
rules.limits: HIGH; the setting, not its content.

rules.meaning: Every .exe / .dll / .sys (or script) file is excluded from scanning.
rules.lookalikes: Practically never legitimate.
rules.limits: HIGH.

rules.meaning: An exclusion entry carries a cheat's name.
rules.limits: At the name rule's severity.

rules.meaning: The Windows DNS cache holds a cheat site's name: the PC looked it up recently.
rules.lookalikes: Curiosity, a link in a chat.
rules.limits: Short-lived; emptied by a restart; DNS-over-HTTPS bypasses it.

rules.meaning: How many cached names were checked.
rules.limits: An empty or small cache is not evidence.

rules.meaning: CPU, GPU, RAM, board, monitors and uptime of the PC.
rules.limits: Self-reported by Windows; useful to recognise the same PC across checks.

rules.meaning: The PC was restarted less than 15 minutes before the check.
rules.lookalikes: Restarting is common and innocent.
rules.limits: Never changes the outcome; only memory-resident state is affected.
